text: There's a new building rule named after you.
openingLine: I just saw the new building rule, and I think we need to talk.

text: Grandma's been banned from the neighborhood group chat.
openingLine: I've brought Grandma over so we can sort out the group chat.

text: The office fridge now has a dress code.
openingLine: I found a dress code on the fridge; do we know who put it there?

text: Someone has brought a plus-one to a job interview.
openingLine: I've brought someone with me to the interview; is that going to be a problem?

text: The restaurant is taking its one-star review personally.
openingLine: I wrote the review, and I'd like to explain what happened.

text: Your roommate wants a performance review.
openingLine: I'd like to understand what you want to cover in my roommate review.

text: The wedding has assigned seating for grudges.
openingLine: I'm looking at the wedding seating plan, and I have a question about my table.

text: You just closed the elevator on your boss.
openingLine: I'm sorry; I didn't realize you were trying to get in.

text: Your neighbor is rehearsing an acceptance speech for a parking space.
openingLine: I can hear you rehearsing from next door; did you get the parking space?

text: The family group chat has appointed a spokesperson.
openingLine: I'd like to know who chose our family spokesperson.

text: The apology came with a loyalty card.
openingLine: I'm trying to apologize, and I don't understand why you've given me this card.

text: Someone has organized a farewell party for a borrowed charger.
openingLine: I still need that charger; can we talk before the farewell party?

text: You brought a store-bought dish and called it homemade.
openingLine: I need to tell you something about the dish I brought.

text: The lost-and-found is holding an auction.
openingLine: I think that's my jacket in the auction.

text: The office plant has its own calendar.
openingLine: I'm trying to book the meeting room, but the plant is already in the calendar.

text: The book club has only read the group chat.
openingLine: I've read the chat, but I haven't actually opened the book.

text: The queue has elected a leader.
openingLine: I've been waiting here for an hour; when did we choose a leader?

text: Someone has reserved a seat for their emotional baggage.
openingLine: I was hoping to sit here; who is this seat reserved for?

text: The bake sale has a complaints department.
openingLine: I'd like to speak to someone about the cake I bought.

text: The house meeting now has a red carpet.
openingLine: I'm here for the house meeting; do I need to take my shoes off?

text: The hotel breakfast has a strict no-boring-hats policy.
openingLine: I came down for breakfast, and nobody mentioned the hat rule.

text: The building's suggestion box has resigned.
openingLine: I came to leave a suggestion, but there's a resignation note on the box.

text: Someone is asking for a refund on a compliment.
openingLine: I'd like to talk about the compliment you gave me yesterday.

text: The neighborhood watch has lost its binoculars.
openingLine: I borrowed the binoculars, and I meant to return them.

text: The first date has requested a second interview.
openingLine: I had a good time, but I'm not sure why you called this another interview.

text: The dating profile has a customer service number.
openingLine: I called the number on your dating profile; was I supposed to?

text: The breakup announcement has a sponsor.
openingLine: I thought we were announcing our breakup privately; who arranged the sponsor?

text: Your date has already planned your next holiday.
openingLine: I'm still choosing dinner; when did we agree on a holiday?

text: The couples therapist has asked for separate reviews.
openingLine: I'm not sure we remember our therapy session the same way.

text: The singles mixer has assigned seating for exes.
openingLine: I've just seen where I'm sitting, and my ex is at that table.

text: The dating app now requires professional references.
openingLine: I'm setting up my dating profile; would you be one of my references?

text: The walk of shame has a concierge.
openingLine: I'm just heading home; could you help me find my coat?

text: The flirting workshop has a waiting list.
openingLine: I thought we could take the flirting class together, but there's only one place left.

text: The honeymoon itinerary has a comments section.
openingLine: I've read the comments on our honeymoon plans; we need to talk about them.

text: Someone is negotiating a friends-with-benefits renewal.
openingLine: I'd like to talk about whether we both still want to keep this casual.

text: The romantic getaway has a shared spreadsheet.
openingLine: I thought we could leave a little of our weekend unplanned.

text: The bachelor party has an HR department.
openingLine: I've been asked to speak to someone about the bachelor party plans.

text: The situationship has scheduled a quarterly review.
openingLine: I'm glad we're talking; I wasn't sure where we stood.

text: Someone has sent a calendar invite for a booty call.
openingLine: I saw your calendar invite; are you asking me to come over tonight?

text: You run into your ex while buying an anniversary gift.
openingLine: I didn't expect to see you here; I'm buying an anniversary gift.

text: The group chat has appointed a treasurer.
openingLine: I'd like to know why our group chat needs a treasurer.

text: Someone has started charging for emotional support in the office.
openingLine: I wanted a quick chat; I didn't realize you were charging for it.

text: The wedding seating plan now has an appeals process.
openingLine: I've seen the seating plan, and I'd like to ask about moving.

text: The neighbors are holding auditions for a new neighbor.
openingLine: I'm here about the apartment; is this really an audition?

text: A restaurant is asking customers for references.
openingLine: I'd like a table for two; what kind of references do you need?

text: Someone brought a PowerPoint to a casual apology.
openingLine: I wanted to hear your apology; do we need the slides?

text: The family is voting on who gets to say “I told you so.”
openingLine: I'd rather we talked about what happened before we take a vote.

text: The book club has finished exactly one paragraph.
openingLine: I've only read the first paragraph; how far did everyone else get?

text: You both claimed the same idea was yours.
openingLine: I heard you present that idea, and I thought it was mine.

text: The apartment viewing includes an interview with the houseplant.
openingLine: I like the apartment; what does the houseplant need to know about me?

text: The carpool has introduced business class.
openingLine: I've been in this carpool for months; why has my seat changed?

text: Someone keeps replying “per my last email” out loud.
openingLine: I'm standing right here; can we just talk about the email?

text: A dinner guest has brought their own feedback form.
openingLine: I'm glad you came for dinner; what's on that form?

text: The dog walker has requested a performance review.
openingLine: I've set aside some time to talk about how the dog walks are going.

text: The potluck spreadsheet has become legally binding.
openingLine: I know I put my name next to salad; can I bring something else?

text: A hotel has introduced a strict no-boring-hats policy.
openingLine: I've just checked in, and I need someone to explain the hat policy.

text: Someone has booked a meeting to discuss fewer meetings.
openingLine: I'm here for the meeting about reducing our meetings.

text: The neighborhood watch is investigating a suspiciously nice lawn.
openingLine: I've noticed you looking at my lawn; is there something you'd like to ask?

text: The birthday wishes have been ranked by effort.
openingLine: I saw where my birthday message came in the ranking.

text: The family photo now requires a rehearsal.
openingLine: I'm ready for the photo; what are we supposed to rehearse?

text: Your boss walks in while you are rehearsing an excuse.
openingLine: I didn't hear you come in; I was practicing what to say to you.

text: A roommate has started issuing invoices for small talk.
openingLine: I found this invoice on my door; can we talk about it?

text: The reunion has a VIP section for people who replied on time.
openingLine: I replied to the reunion invite; am I at the right entrance?

text: Someone has hired a spokesperson for the group chat.
openingLine: I think we need to replace Diana; she keeps telling the group chat the wrong thing.

text: The wedding DJ is taking requests by formal application.
openingLine: I'd like to request a song; where do I put this application?

text: The shared fridge has elected a representative.
openingLine: I came to get my lunch; who's representing the fridge?

text: The dating app has added a references section.
openingLine: I've reached the references section of this dating app, and I need your help.

text: The exes at the wedding have formed a table committee.
openingLine: I'm at the exes' table; did we all agree to sit together?

text: The speed-dating event now has a complaints desk.
openingLine: I'd like to talk to someone about how the speed dating went.

text: A first date has brought a printed agenda.
openingLine: I'm glad we finally met; what's on the agenda you brought?

text: Someone has requested a probation period before becoming exclusive.
openingLine: I'd like us to be exclusive, but I need to understand what you're proposing.

text: A dating profile has been sent back for revisions.
openingLine: I've had my profile sent back again; can we look at the changes?

text: One of you has told everyone you are a couple.
openingLine: I've had three people congratulate me; what have you told them?

text: The breakup text has been workshopped by six friends.
openingLine: I wanted to talk to you directly about the breakup text.

text: The singles mixer has assigned a project manager.
openingLine: I'm new to this singles mixer; who put you in charge?

text: A flirty message has accidentally become a team discussion.
openingLine: I sent that message to one person; how did we all end up discussing it?

text: The romantic getaway has a chore rota.
openingLine: I thought this weekend was a break; can we talk about the chore rota?

text: The dating app bio now needs two professional references.
openingLine: I'm updating my dating bio; would you be comfortable giving me a reference?

text: A love triangle has requested a scheduling app.
openingLine: I'd like to find a time when the three of us can talk.

text: Someone has put “good at texting back” on their résumé.
openingLine: I'm looking at your résumé; could you explain the texting skill?

text: The couple’s matching outfits require written approval.
openingLine: I thought we were choosing our own clothes tonight.

text: The honeymoon itinerary has been reviewed by an ex.
openingLine: I'd like to know why your ex has seen our honeymoon plans.

text: A first kiss has been postponed by a calendar conflict.
openingLine: I'd still like to kiss you; when are we both actually free?

text: The anniversary gift comes with a customer satisfaction survey.
openingLine: I opened your gift; do you really want me to fill out the survey?

text: The date has asked everyone to keep their flirting receipts.
openingLine: I'm not sure what you want me to keep from our date.

text: A situationship has introduced quarterly check-ins.
openingLine: I'm glad we made time to talk about what this is.

text: The romantic playlist has been returned with notes.
openingLine: I made that playlist for us; can we listen to it together?

text: Someone has made a spreadsheet of mixed signals.
openingLine: I'd rather hear how you feel than try to read this spreadsheet.

text: The awkward morning-after chat has minutes and action items.
openingLine: I thought we could have breakfast and talk about last night.

text: You agreed to keep it casual. One of you made anniversary plans.
openingLine: I thought we were keeping this casual; what are the anniversary plans?

text: You each thought the other person was paying for the first date.
openingLine: I thought you were treating me tonight; did we get our wires crossed?

text: Your date arrives wearing the sweater you donated last week.
openingLine: I think I used to own that sweater; where did you find it?

text: You discover your date has already met all your friends without you.
openingLine: I was going to introduce you, but you seem to know everyone.

text: Your ex asks for the spare key while your new date is at the door.
openingLine: I know you need the key back; can we make this quick?

text: You both booked the same restaurant for separate dates.
openingLine: I didn't expect to see you here with someone else.

text: Your date calls your bluff about being a great dancer.
openingLine: I may have overstated the dancing part; would you still like to try?

text: You accidentally bring a packed overnight bag to a coffee date.
openingLine: I can explain the bag; I wasn't assuming anything.

text: Your date thinks the flowers in your hand are for them.
openingLine: I should probably explain who these flowers are for.

text: You find out you have been flirting with each other under different app names.
openingLine: I think we've already had this conversation on the app.

text: Your date suggests splitting dessert just as you order two.
openingLine: I've ordered my own; did you want us to share?

text: You arrive at a singles night with the ex who gave you a ride.
openingLine: I'm grateful for the lift, but how are we introducing ourselves?

text: Your friend introduces you to the person you kissed last weekend.
openingLine: I think we can skip the introduction; we met on Saturday.

text: Your date has mistaken your work story for a marriage proposal.
openingLine: I was talking about a work project; what did you hear?

text: You invite a date over and discover your roommate is hosting your ex.
openingLine: I didn't know we were both having company tonight.

text: You and your date both pretend not to recognize the love song.
openingLine: I know this song; is it the one we talked about?

text: Your date asks why your dating profile is still getting updates.
openingLine: I thought we were still seeing other people; can we talk about it?

text: You are returning an ex's things and neither of you claims the good coat.
openingLine: I thought this coat was yours; do we know whose it is?

text: Your date remembers the joke you used on a previous date with them.
openingLine: I have told you that story already, haven't I?

text: You tell a date you love cooking just before the takeaway arrives.
openingLine: I need to admit something before I answer the door.

text: You both brought a friend to what each called a casual drink.
openingLine: I brought someone so this would feel casual; I see you did too.

text: Your date wants a photo together before you have learned their surname.
openingLine: I'd like to know a little more about you before we post anything.

text: You accept a second date, then realize it is an all-day hike.
openingLine: I'd like to see you again; how long is this walk?

text: Your ex wants to keep the dinner reservation after the breakup.
openingLine: I know it's hard to get a table there; are we really going together?

text: Your date has been practicing your name and still gets it wrong.
openingLine: I heard you practicing; would it help if I said it again?

text: You both reach to hold hands and end up carrying each other's shopping.
openingLine: I was actually reaching for your hand.

text: Your crush asks you to help choose an outfit for another date.
openingLine: I can help with the outfit, but I should tell you something first.

text: Your date arrives early while you are rehearsing the greeting.
openingLine: I didn't expect you yet; how much of that did you hear?

text: You invite someone for a romantic picnic and bring the wrong lunch bag.
openingLine: I packed us a picnic, but this isn't the bag I prepared.

text: You and your date disagree about whether this is your third or fourth date.
openingLine: I'm counting tonight as number four; which one am I missing?

text: Your ex joins the same dance class you signed up for with a new date.
openingLine: I didn't know you'd be here; I'm taking the class with someone.

text: Your date asks you to explain the heart you drew on their receipt.
openingLine: I put that heart there on purpose; I wasn't sure if you'd notice.

text: You both try to leave a party last so you can ask each other out.
openingLine: I'd like to stay and talk to you, but we could also go somewhere.

text: You agreed to a casual overnight stay, but someone has brought breakfast for the week.
openingLine: I thought you were staying one night; how many breakfasts are in that bag?

text: You and a casual partner both pretend not to have left a toothbrush behind.
openingLine: I found a toothbrush here, and I think we should talk about it.

text: You are dividing shared belongings after a breakup and both want the expensive sheets.
openingLine: I'd like to keep these sheets; what were you hoping to take?

text: Your partner thought the romantic hotel booking included separate rooms.
openingLine: I booked one room for us; would you prefer me to change it?

text: You planned a private anniversary evening, but your partner invited another couple to dinner.
openingLine: I thought tonight would just be us; when did we invite company?

text: You and your ex have separate dates at the hotel you booked before breaking up.
openingLine: I thought you would have canceled your half of the booking.

text: You arrive for an agreed sleepover with a pillow your host recognizes from their ex's home.
openingLine: I brought my own pillow; why are you looking at it like that?

text: A casual partner offers you a drawer just as you suggest seeing other people.
openingLine: I appreciate the drawer, but I wanted to talk about keeping things casual.

text: You both assumed the other person had told your housemate about the overnight guest.
openingLine: I thought you knew I was staying; should we sort this out?

text: You and your partner disagree about what the shared holiday fund can pay for.
openingLine: I thought the holiday fund was for the trip, not this purchase.

text: Your partner finds the romantic note you were drafting before a serious money talk.
openingLine: I wrote that earlier; can we talk about both things tonight?

text: You agree to move in together, then discover neither of you plans to leave your own apartment.
openingLine: I thought we were moving into your place; what did you have in mind?

text: You meet a casual partner for brunch and both introduce someone else as a date.
openingLine: I didn't know we'd be making introductions this morning.

text: You planned a weekend alone together, but neither of you can stop checking house listings.
openingLine: I'd like us to put the phones down; are we house hunting or having a weekend away?

text: Your ex wants to buy your share of the sofa in tiny monthly payments.
openingLine: I'd like to settle the sofa today; what can we work out?

text: You call someone your partner while they are explaining that you keep things casual.
openingLine: I called you my partner; I think we need to decide what we're saying.

text: You and your partner discover you each quietly renewed a different dating-app subscription.
openingLine: I renewed mine too; can we talk honestly about what we both want?

text: You buy a romantic gift together and disagree about whose card should pay.
openingLine: I thought this was a gift for both of us; how are we paying for it?

text: You are collecting things after a breakup and find the bag packed with your current partner's belongings.
openingLine: I came for my things, but this looks like the wrong bag.

text: You both agreed to a discreet relationship and arrive at the same dinner wearing matching rings.
openingLine: I didn't know you'd wear yours tonight; what are we telling people?

text: You extend a romantic weekend and then remember you both work from the same small room.
openingLine: I'd love another day here; how do we handle our calls in one room?

text: A planned night together begins with a disagreement about which ex owns the spare bedding.
openingLine: I can make up the bed; do we actually own these sheets?

text: You and your partner compare what each thought your couples' savings account was for.
openingLine: I thought we were saving for a home; what did you want to use it for?

text: Your casual partner asks to be your emergency contact while you are finding your shoes.
openingLine: I'm happy to talk about that, but I thought we were keeping things casual.

text: You and an ex share a hotel loyalty account, and both want the anniversary upgrade.
openingLine: I used the points for this room; did you have plans for them too?

text: You plan a quiet morning after an agreed sleepover, but a furniture delivery arrives.
openingLine: I was going to make us coffee; did you order a bed for today?

text: You and your partner each bought an expensive surprise trip for the same weekend.
openingLine: I booked us a trip; please tell me yours is for another weekend.

text: You have agreed to stop seeing each other, but your clothes are still in the wash together.
openingLine: I'd like my things back, but I can wait for the wash to finish.

text: You invite a casual partner to stay and realize you have framed their forgotten shopping list.
openingLine: I liked having a reminder of you here; is the frame too much?

text: Your partner wants to discuss moving in while you are returning the spare key.
openingLine: I brought the key back because I thought we were taking a step back.

text: You both arrive at a couples' weekend expecting it to be a breakup conversation.
openingLine: I came prepared to talk about ending things; what were you hoping for?

text: You agree to keep separate finances, then receive a joint invoice for your romantic getaway.
openingLine: I asked for separate bills; can we work out who booked what?
